chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who confessed upon himself for a Hadd (fixed penalty), and did not specify which Hadd it was. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is ordered to be whipped until he is the one who prevents the Hadd from himself [by specifying it].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone confesses to a Hadd penalty but does not specify which one?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) is applied to ensure justice when a confessor remains vague; the individual is not released until they clarify their guilt, preventing them from exploiting ambiguity to avoid the specific *Hadd*. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the confessor's active role in defining their own liability, ensuring that the punishment matches the actual offense rather than a generic assumption. It highlights the balance between strict adherence to fixed penalties and the procedural fairness required in Islamic courts.
